                      Drake Sword | Dark Souls Wiki



                      Drake Sword +5
                      300 100
                      - 32
                      - 360
                      - 6.0
                      Requirements & Bonus
                      16 10 – –
                      Weapon Type Straight Sword
                      Attack Type Regular
                      Enchantable No
                      Special Yes
                       

                      Drake Sword is a Weapon in Dark Souls. This weapon is one of the most powerful options early in the game, offering significant damage that outclasses most weapons at that stage. However, it lacks the stat scaling and upgrade potential that other weapons possess, meaning it may be outperformed later in the game. You can obtain this weapon by cutting off the tail of the Hellkite Wyvern in Undead Burg.

                       

                      This sword, one of the rare dragon weapons, is formed by a drake's tail. Drakes are seen as undeveloped imitators of the dragons, but they are likely their distant kin."
                      "The sword is imbued with a mystical power, to be released when held with both hands."

                       

                      How to Get the Drake Sword in Dark Souls

                      • Obtained by cutting off the tail of Hellkite Wyvern in the Undead Burg (either by fighting him normally or by shooting off his tail with a bow and arrows from below the bridge).

                       

                      Dark Souls Drake Sword Hints and Tips:

                      • Can be given to Kingseeker Frampt to receive 5,000 Souls.
                      • Drake Sword can be upgraded by using Dragon Scales.
                      • When equipped grants Magic DEF +15 and Flame DEF +15.
                      • It's not recommended to spend Dragon Scales and 10,000 Souls per upgrade on this weapon as the resulting low increase in damage does not offset the high cost.
                      • Decent weapon at the earliest point it can be procured thanks to high base damage with low stat requirements. As it doesn't scale with any stats and upgrading it has little effect in exchange for scarce upgrade material, it should be replaced early on. After reaching Andre and when reaching the point of being able to upgrade weapons to +5, it should be permanently ignored.
                      • If you wield it with two hands, pressing or holding (stronger attack) R2 will trigger a shockwave attack. Do note that every use of this attack consumes 30 durability points of your weapon. You can use this attack 12 times until this sword's durability drops to 0 points and it breaks.
                      • Can be traded to Frampt for 5,000 souls; useful for when it is made irrelevant by higher scaling weapons. Be warned that if you intend to get the Knight's Honor achievement you will need to acquire this sword.

                       

                      Dark Souls Drake Sword Lore

                      • The Drake Sword is part of a theme that ties the Everlasting Dragons to stone.
                      • A blade similar to the Drake Sword is used by Pthumerians, and Martyr Logarius, in Bloodborne.

                                            PSA: If you're a beginner contemplating getting this thing, READ THIS. There's a better option that will serve you far better and longer than the Drake Sword.

                                            It's the Claymore sitting right at the end of the bridge where the Hellkite Drake is, the very same creature who's tail you're about to shoot off. It has the EXACT same stat requirements as the Drake Sword.

                                            Instead of using that bow and arrow you bought to get the Drake Sword, stand at the the stairs that lead down to the underside of the bridge. Bait out its fire attack, and when its done, come back out and fire an arrow at the Drake. It'll jump down onto the Bridge to fight. Simply run past it and grab the claymore. You can also grab the bonefire in the altar. The Drake should fly off once you rest at the bonfire (don't worry, it'll come back if you're insistent on getting the Drake Sword, just reload the game). Progress in the game, normally. Yes, the Claymore isn't as powerful off the bat, but it should still serve well enough and it will get much more powerful quickly.

                                            Eventually, you'll reach Andre the Blacksmith. By the time you do, you SHOULD have some titanite shards. Use them to upgrade the Claymore as much as you can. He also sells Titanite Shards for relatively cheap, so feel free to buy some or just farm them off enemies (or just farm souls to buy them). Pretty soon, you should have a +5 Claymore that does a base damage of 154. But, with small investments into dex, the damage bonus you get from your stats should push it close if not past 200, the base damage of the Drake Sword.

                                            Congratulations! You're doing just as much damage as you would have with the Drake Sword and you have a weapon that will serve you longer with its good scaling! It'll keep getting better the more you level up! And once you get the Large Ember from the Depths, you'll REALLY be in business! You can farm the blob monsters in the Depths for Large Titanite Shards that, combined with the Large Ember, will get your weapon to +10. Don't forget to put some levels into Strength and Dexterity. Don't just dump everything into Vitality and Endurance!

                                              Honestly, the Drake Sword is probably one of the most iconic weapons in the entire game.

                                              So, so many of us struggled greatly during our first playthrough; in the Undead Burg, against the Taurus Demon, etc. The game was such a slog, every death sending you back and you'd desperately battle through the same enemies you're still learning to fight to try and get your precious souls back only to get killed and watch all your hard work disappear. So many deaths, over and over again. You said you weren't gonna look up guides, but if you see "You Died" appear on your screen one more time, you might throw yourself out the nearest window. You HAVE to find something that can help you.

                                              And then, after scrolling on Google, you find a guide that tells of a hidden sword dropped by that Dragon at the bridge that killed you so many times. The sword does MASSIVE damage and only requires 16 Str and 10 dex to use! You're already WELL beyond that! And, best of all, you don't even have to KILL the dragon! All you need is a bow and some arrows and shoot the tail from the safety of the pathway beneath the bridge. You hurry to the Undead Merchant, then race to the Dragon and, after a few minutes of shooting at its tail...it's yours: The Drake Sword.

                                              The moveset feels good, it has a shockwave attack that PLOWS through groups of enemies, and, most importantly, it kills EVERYTHING in a couple of hits. This thing is AMAZING. Finally...you're actually making PROGRESS when you were on the verge of uninstalling this god-forsaken game only a few moments ago. Suddenly, the prospect of actually beating this game seems possible!

                                              Eventually you find a blacksmith in a building and he can upgrade your weapons! EEEE! You better believe I'm upgrading my bad boy, The Drake Sword. Ah...but you need Dragon Scales and 10,000 Souls :( . Well...no surprise it's expensive. It's probably one of the most powerful weapons in the game! You consider upgrading some other weapons, but it'll take SO MANY upgrades for them to even MATCH the awesome power of the Drake Sword, and they don't have that cool shockwave attack! So screw that! Let's just invest in more health and stamina, so we can tank more hits, attack more, and be able to carry the Drake Sword AND your Heater Shield.

                                              It would be a beautiful time you'd spend...until eventually, you would encounter Sen's Fortress or Anor Londo. It is only then that you realize that you might have made a terrible mistake.

                                                            Some alternatives for Drake Sword if you want to have strong weapon at the begining.

                                                            1) Fire Zweihander / Uchigatana / Great Scythe / Great Club / Reinforced Club / some_other_strong_weapon_you_can_find_early. Do suicide running around getting items, soul items and green titanites, get to Vamos, buy shards, upgrade to +5 then ascend to Fire. It can be done after Asylum if you have Master Key and you can get it to +5 Fire even before Burg if you want to farm some easy to kill leeches in Blighttown swamp. While fire weapons deal split damage they're superior at early locations.

                                                            2) Demon's Spear. Do suicide running around getting soul items, buy Crest of Artorias, farm Forest Hunters, join Forest Hunters, buy it from Shiva. Trade 1 Prism Stone and 1 Dung Pie from Female Undead Merchant with Snuggly to have +2 weapon. It can be done after Asylum if you have Master Key. Again despite dealing split damage it's superior for early locations.

                                                            3) Gravelord Sword. Do suicide run into the Catacombs to pick Eyes of Death, jump into nearby coffin, join Gravelord Servants and you get this, upgrade same way as in point 2. If you skip upgrading part you can do it even without Master Key right after Asylum. This time it's pure physical damage and Toxin effect for free.

                                                            But mostly important do not let other people tell you how to play. If you love Drake Sword just use it, nothing wrong with that. I'm only writing this to point out that there are other powerful one-shot killing options you can get very early.

                                                                    This is a good starter weapon, regardless of build. Almost every time I start a new playthrough I use this because it's easy to get early and is super effective in the early game. But it doesn't scale with your character, so it's not very helpful after the first third of the game.

                                                                    The sword does 200 damage per hit. That's really good at the start! The boss that you'll likely fight after getting this can be killed in like five hits with this sword. As you get deeper into the game the enemies you fight will get more and more HP, but the Drake Sword will still only deal 200 damage. Most of the other weapons scale with your stats like dexterity and strength, so as you become stronger your weapon becomes stronger, but the Drake Sword doesn't scale at all.

                                                                    You can upgrade the sword to make it deal 300 damage, but that won't make much of a difference in the late game. Especially since the materials you need to upgrade it are rare, in limited supply, and don't appear until half way through the game. You're better off just switching to different weapon that will scale with your character stats and upgrading that instead. I always use this sword to carry me through the first third of the game as I level up and acquire materials to upgrade something else to use for the mid and late game.

                                                                                        I've used this for a few areas on my recent sl4 (hunter) run, and that's not something I ever expected to say. It makes the cut as part of my arsenal because, quite simply, it's actually pretty hard to find a decent weapon that can hit 300 phys AR with base stats.

                                                                                        A lightning claymore may be able to hit about 500 AR, but that damage is split, and it swings relatively slowly in comparison.

                                                                                        Quelaag's fury sword hits just under 400 AR with max humanity, but once again, almost 300 of that is fire damage.

                                                                                        Jagged ghost blade caps out just under 240, swings faster and has bleed... yet it can't multihit from a distance.

                                                                                        The drake sword though... it can be two-handed with base hunter stats, it takes out the bloat-headed bastards in Oolacile in two hits, and it can use a multi-target straight line pseudo AoE.

                                                                                        It's no chaos gargoyle hally, but it breaks the endless monotony of reinforced clubbing on low level runs when you need pure physical damage.

                                                                                        I've been playing this game since the PC release, haven't touched it since my first playthrough (abandoned that character), but damn... it's not actually complete garbage, even in the late game. I just sucked when I used to hate on it and never returned to it.

                                                                                        The extra 50 or so damage over other straight swords really matters when scaling isn't a (noticeable) factor, and it makes this thing out-damage some of the staple elemental choices against resistant mobs. I still wouldn't call it "good", especially in a normal run, but it's certainly passable if you're willing to kill some drakes (which drop scales pretty frequently with 10 humanity and CGSR if you're offline).

                                                                                                                                      But if you prefer more casual style (focused on finishing areas one by one and taking the normal route) the Drake Sword is very easy to get and really good weapon for early areas (both Burgs, Parish, Dephts and Darkroot) since it's basic damage is higher than most weapons upgraded to +5.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     I'm in the endgame and this is still my primary weapon.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                    I use it with one or with both hands, depending on situation.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                    (I am often switching during the same fight -- 'offensive with two hands' or 'defensive with one hand plus shield'.)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                    I am very agile and quick with it and I yield a high ratio of 'damage per second'.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                    It has a good range and a "round up" movement set on *one hand heavy attack*.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Its a mercyless slasher with *two hand light attack*.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                    I have more endurance than health points (31 vs 34), so I can land at least 5 swings in a row without exhausting)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                    All regular enemies are down after a 'one hit', inkl. bigger standard enemies.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Sentinels in Darkroot Garden take 4 hits and those in Anor Londo take 5 hits.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                    So I am done with all of them in an instant and mostly without taking any damage myself.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                    I just finished boss fight "4 Kings" on my very first attempt.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                    I don't think its true, that this sword is only for the early game.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                    I intent to use it for the whole run.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Its great together with pyromancy.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                    I have a devine uchigatana as a second weapon, but it is definitely weaker (+10, dex 32, fth 16).
